output:
ADIB's consolidated six-month income table on physical page 4 is an embedded image; I rendered and read it. Income from Islamic financing of EGP29,117,908 thousand less deposit and similar costs of EGP16,863,967 thousand equals net income from funds of EGP12,253,941 thousand. The signed expected-credit-loss income-statement effect is -EGP2,176 thousand: a net charge, not a release. This is distinct from the three-month release of EGP78,142 thousand. Combining the latter with the half-year charge implies a first-quarter net charge of EGP80,318 thousand, illustrating how a small net half-year amount can mask offsetting movements.

For an Islamic bank, funding income and deposit costs describe the earnings engine, but net funds income is an amount, not a financing margin or credit-risk denominator. Positive earnings and the quarter's release are supportive counterevidence against assuming uniformly worsening credit costs; neither proves clean financing assets. Cost of risk needs a defined credit-loss numerator and matching average gross financing exposure, period/annualization convention, and ECL reconciliation. Stage migration, nonperforming financing, coverage, recoveries and write-offs are missing from the admitted page. I would retain ADIB for credit-quality research, withhold a cost-of-risk ratio, and make no investment or trade clearance from this statement alone. The document period and retained capture do not establish first public availability.
